# Duc - Disk Usage Checker

Duc is a collection of tools for indexing, inspecting and visualizing disk
usage. Duc maintains a database of accumulated sizes of directories of the file
system, and allows you to query this database with some tools, or create fancy
graphs showing you where your bytes are.

![duc gui](/img/palette-rainbow.png) 

## What is Duc?

Duc is a tool that helps you understand where your disk space is being used. It:

- Indexes your file system to track directory sizes
- Provides multiple interfaces to query and visualize disk usage
- Scales well (tested on systems with 500+ million files and petabytes of storage)
- Creates beautiful sunburst graphs to visualize space usage

## Usage

### Creating an Index

Before you can view disk usage information, you need to create an index:

```bash
duc index /usr
```

This will scan the specified directory and store size information in a database
(default location: `$HOME/.duc.db`).

### Querying the Index

Duc provides several commands to explore your disk usage:

- **`duc info`** - Show available directory trees in the database
- **`duc ls`** - List files and directories with their sizes
- **`duc ui`** - Interactive ncurses-based console interface
- **`duc gui`** - Graphical (X11) sunburst graph interface
- **`duc graph`** - Generate static graph images
- **`duc cgi`** - Web interface via CGI
- **`duc histogram`** - Show file size distribution
- **`duc topn`** - Show largest files
- **`duc xml`** - Export data as XML
- **`duc json`** - Export data as JSON

### Examples

Index your home directory:
```bash
duc index ~
```

List the top-level directories:
```bash
duc ls /
```

Launch the interactive UI:
```bash
duc ui /
```

Create a graph image:
```bash
duc graph /usr > /tmp/duc-graph.png
```

### Configuration

Duc can be configured via configuration files at:
- `/etc/ducrc`
- `~/.config/duc/ducrc`
- `~/.ducrc`
- `./.ducrc`

You can also set the database location using the `DUC_DATABASE` environment variable.

### Common Options

Most duc commands support these options:

- `-d`, `--database=FILE` - Specify database file location
- `-b`, `--bytes` - Show exact byte counts
- `-h`, `--help` - Show help information
- `-v`, `--verbose` - Increase output verbosity
- `-q`, `--quiet` - Quiet mode

### Indexing Options

When creating an index with `duc index`:

- `-e`, `--exclude=PATTERN` - Exclude files matching pattern
- `-x`, `--one-file-system` - Don't cross filesystem boundaries
- `-p`, `--progress` - Show progress during indexing
- `-H`, `--check-hard-links` - Count hard links only once
- `-m`, `--max-depth=N` - Limit directory depth stored in database
- `-u`, `--username=USER` - Index only files owned by specific user

### Visualization Options

For graphical commands (`duc gui`, `duc graph`):

- `--palette=SCHEME` - Color scheme (rainbow, greyscale, monochrome, size)
- `--fuzz=FACTOR` - Adjust visual size calculation
- `--levels=N` - Number of directory levels to show
- `--size=WxH` - Output image size

## More Information

For complete documentation including all commands and options, please refer to
the user manual (`duc.1` man page) in the `doc/` directory.

Check the Duc homepage at http://duc.zevv.nl for additional information.
---manual---

duc(1) -- index, query and graph disk usage
===========================================

## SYNOPSIS

`duc` <subcommand> [options]


## DESCRIPTION

Duc is a collection of tools for inspecting and visualizing disk usage.

duc(1) -- index, query and graph disk usage
===========================================

## SYNOPSIS

`duc` <subcommand> [options]


## DESCRIPTION

Duc is a collection of tools for inspecting and visualizing disk usage. 

Duc maintains an indexed database of accumulated sizes of directories of your
file system, and allows you to query this database with some tools, or create
fancy sunburst graphs to show you where your bytes are.

Duc scales quite well, it has been tested on systems with more than 500 million
files and several petabytes of storage. 


## USAGE

Duc comes with a command line tool called `duc`, which is used to create,
maintain and query the disk usage database.  run `duc help` to get a list of
available commands. `duc help <subcommand>` describes the usage of a specific
subcommand. Run `duc help --all` for an extensive list of all commands and
their options.

Some commands might not be available on your system, depending on the exact
configuration chosen when building Duc. (For example, the `duc gui` command is
not available in the `duc-nox` package on Debian and Ubuntu)

Duc allows any option to be placed either on the command line or in a
configuration file. Options on the command line are preceded by a
double-leading-dash (`--option`), some options have a corresponding short
option which can be used as well with a single leading dash. (`-o`)

At startup duc tries to read its configuration from three locations in this
particular order: `/etc/ducrc`, `~/.config/duc/ducrc`, `~/.ducrc` and
`./.ducrc`.

A configuration file consists of sections and parameters. The section names
correspond to the duc subcommands for which the parameters in that section
apply. A section begins with the name of the section in square brackets and
continues until the next section begins. Sections contain parameters, one per
line, which consist of a single option name for boolean flags, or an option name
and a value for options which take a value. See the EXAMPLES section for an
example of the configuration file format.


## CREATING THE INDEX

Duc needs an index file of the file system before it is able to show any
information.  To create the index, run the `duc index` command. For example, to
create an index of your home directory run `duc index ~`

    $ duc index /usr
    Skipping lost+found: Permission denied
    Indexed 333823 files and 48200 directories, (35.0GB total) in 1 seconds

The default location of the database is `$HOME/.duc.db`. To use a different
database location, use the DUC_DATABASE environment variable or specify the
database location with the --database argument.

You can run `duc index` at any time later to rebuild the index.

By default Duc indexes all directories it encounters during file system
traversal, including special file systems like /proc and /sys, and
network file systems like NFS or Samba mounts. There are a few options to
select what parts of your filesystem you want to include or exclude from the
scan, check the documentation below for the options --one-file-system, 
--exclude, --fs-exclude and --fs-include for more details.


## QUERYING THE INDEX

Duc has various subcommands for querying or exploring the index: (Note that
depending on your configuration, some of these commands might not be available)

* `duc info` shows a list of available directory trees in the database, and the time
  and date of the last scan.

* `duc ls` lists all files and directories under the given path on the console.

* `duc ui` runs a ncurses based console user interface for exploring the file
  system usage.

* `duc gui` starts a graphical (X11) interface representing the file system in
  a sunburst graph. Click on a directory to redraw the graph from the
  perspective of the selected directory. Click in the center of the graph to go
  up one directory in the tree.


## OPTIONS

This section list all available subcommands and describes their usage and options.

### Global options

These options apply to all Duc subcommands:

  * `--debug`:
    increase verbosity to debug level

  * `-h`, `--help`:
    show help

  * `-q`, `--quiet`:
    quiet mode, do not print any warning

  * `-v`, `--verbose`:
    increase verbosity

  * `--version`:
    output version information and exit

### duc help

Options for command `duc help [options]`:

  * `-a`, `--all`:
    show complete help for all commands

### duc index

The 'index' subcommand performs a recursive scan of the given paths on the
filesystem and calculates the inclusive size of all directories. The results
are written to the index, and can later be queried by one of the other duc tools.


Options for command `duc index [options] PATH ...`:

  * `-b`, `--bytes`:
    show file size in exact number of bytes

  * `-d`, `--database=VAL`:
    use database file VAL

  * `-e`, `--exclude=VAL`:
    exclude files matching VAL

  * `-H`, `--check-hard-links`:

## FREQUENTLY ASKED QUESTIONS

* What does the error 'Database version mismatch mean?'
 
  The layout of the index database sometimes changes when new features are
  implemented. When you get this error you have probably upgraded to a newer
  version. Just remove the old database file and rebuild the index.

* Duc crashes with a segmentation fault, is it that buggy?

  By default Duc uses the Tokyocabinet database backend. Tokyocabinet is pretty
  fast, stores the database in a single file and has nice compression support
  to keep the database small. Unfortunately, it is not always robust and
  sometimes chokes on corrupt database files. Try to remove the database
  and rebuild the index. If the error persists contact the authors.

* Some of the Duc subcommands like `duc gui` are not available on my system?

  Depending on the configuration that was chosen when building Duc, some
  options might or might not be available in the `duc` utility. For example, on
  Debian or Ubuntu Duc comes in two flavours: there is a full featured package
  called `duc`, or a package without dependencies on X-windows called
  `duc-nox`, for which the latter lacks the `duc gui` command.

* `duc index` is hogging my system and using a lot of CPU and I/O!

  Traversing a file system is hard work - which is the exact reason why Duc
  exists in the first place. You can use the default tools to make Duc behave
  nice towards other processes on your machine, use something like:

  `nice 19 ionice -c 3 duc index [options]`

  This makes `duc index` run with the lowest CPU and I/O scheduler priorities,
  which is nicer to all the other processes on your machine.


## FILES

At startup duc tries to read its configuration from three locations in this
particular order: `/etc/ducrc`, `~/.config/duc/ducrc`, `~/.ducrc` and
`./.ducrc`.

Duc mainains an index of scanned directories, which defaults to ~/.duc.db. All tools
take the -d/--database option to override the database path.

duc(1) -- index, query and graph disk usage
===========================================

## SYNOPSIS

`duc` <subcommand> [options]


## DESCRIPTION

Duc is a collection of tools for inspecting and visualizing disk usage. 

Duc maintains an indexed database of accumulated sizes of directories of your
file system, and allows you to query this database with some tools, or create
fancy sunburst graphs to show you where your bytes are.

Duc scales quite well, it has been tested on systems with more than 500 million
files and several petabytes of storage. 


## USAGE

Duc comes with a command line tool called `duc`, which is used to create,
maintain and query the disk usage database.  run `duc help` to get a list of
available commands. `duc help <subcommand>` describes the usage of a specific
subcommand. Run `duc help --all` for an extensive list of all commands and
their options.

Some commands might not be available on your system, depending on the exact
configuration chosen when building Duc. (For example, the `duc gui` command is
not available in the `duc-nox` package on Debian and Ubuntu)

Duc allows any option to be placed either on the command line or in a
configuration file. Options on the command line are preceded by a
double-leading-dash (`--option`), some options have a corresponding short
option which can be used as well with a single leading dash. (`-o`)

At startup duc tries to read its configuration from three locations in this
particular order: `/etc/ducrc`, `~/.config/duc/ducrc`, `~/.ducrc` and
`./.ducrc`.

A configuration file consists of sections and parameters. The section names
correspond to the duc subcommands for which the parameters in that section
apply. A section begins with the name of the section in square brackets and
continues until the next section begins. Sections contain parameters, one per
line, which consist of a single option name for boolean flags, or an option name
and a value for options which take a value. See the EXAMPLES section for an
example of the configuration file format.


## CREATING THE INDEX

Duc needs an index file of the file system before it is able to show any
information.  To create the index, run the `duc index` command. For example, to
create an index of your home directory run `duc index ~`

    $ duc index /usr
    Skipping lost+found: Permission denied
    Indexed 333823 files and 48200 directories, (35.0GB total) in 1 seconds

The default location of the database is `$HOME/.duc.db`. To use a different
database location, use the DUC_DATABASE environment variable or specify the
database location with the --database argument.

You can run `duc index` at any time later to rebuild the index.

By default Duc indexes all directories it encounters during file system
traversal, including special file systems like /proc and /sys, and
network file systems like NFS or Samba mounts. There are a few options to
select what parts of your filesystem you want to include or exclude from the
scan, check the documentation below for the options --one-file-system, 
--exclude, --fs-exclude and --fs-include for more details.


## QUERYING THE INDEX

Duc has various subcommands for querying or exploring the index: (Note that
depending on your configuration, some of these commands might not be available)

* `duc info` shows a list of available directory trees in the database, and the time
  and date of the last scan.

* `duc ls` lists all files and directories under the given path on the console.

* `duc ui` runs a ncurses based console user interface for exploring the file
  system usage.

* `duc gui` starts a graphical (X11) interface representing the file system in
  a sunburst graph. Click on a directory to redraw the graph from the
  perspective of the selected directory. Click in the center of the graph to go
  up one directory in the tree.


## OPTIONS

This section list all available subcommands and describes their usage and options.

>>>> run duc help --all for a list of all subcommands and options.


## CGI INTERFACING

The `duc` binary has support for a rudimentary CGI interface, currently only
tested with apache.  The CGI interface generates a simple HTML page with a list
of indexed directories, and shows a clickable graph for navigating the file
system. If the option `--list` is given, a list of top sized files/dirs is also
written.

Configuration is done by creating a simple shell script as .cgi in a directory
which is configured for CGI execution by your web server (usually
`/usr/lib/cgi-bin`). The shell script should simply start duc, and pass the
location of the database to navigate.

An example duc.cgi script would be

    #!/bin/sh
    /usr/local/bin/duc cgi -d /home/jenny/.duc.db

* Make sure the database file is readable by the user (usually www-data)
* Debugging is best done by inspecting the web server's error log
* Make sure the .cgi script has execute permissions (`chmod +x duc.cgi`)

Some notes:

* The HTML page is generated with a simple embedded CSS

# Now we need to design final implementation in Python.
# Steps:
# - Parse global options and subcommand
# - Read config files
# - Merge options: config global + config subcommand + env var + command line
# - Database handling: Our own sqlite with table blobs
# Implementation of DB:
# We'll create table blobs(key PRIMARY KEY, value BLOB)
# Keys:
# - "duc_version" -> version string? Not needed.
# - "duc_index_reports" -> JSON list of report entries? We'll store as JSON blob for simplicity.
# - For each indexed path, key = path itself (like "/tmp/testduc") -> value = JSON encoding of metadata: {path, dev, ino, time, files, dirs, size_apparent, size_actual, histogram, topn, ...}
# - For each directory, key = f"{dev}/{ino:x}" -> value = JSON encoding of dir content: {dev, ino, size_apparent, size_actual, count_files, count_dirs, entries: [{name, type, size_apparent, size_actual, dev, ino, count?}, ...]}
# This will be sufficient for our operations.
# We also need histogram storage: we can compute histogram on the fly from files, or store per report.
# Simpler: For each indexed path, store histogram array as part of its report.
# For topn: store list of largest files.

# Let's design data structures:
# During index:
# - Walk filesystem recursively, for each directory create DucDir object.
# - DucDir: path, dev, ino, entries (list), size_apparent, size_actual, file_count, dir_count, total_count (files+dirs recursively)
# - For each file: stat, get apparent size = st_size, actual = st_blocks*512
# - For dirs, we need to handle hard links: maintain set of (dev, ino) seen, if -H and already seen, skip.
# - Exclude patterns: use fnmatch? Test with "*file1" pattern: "*file1" should match "file1" or path? Let's assume fnmatch on basename and full path.
# - one-file-system: if -x, skip dirs where st_dev != root dev.
# - uid/username: check st_uid, and if username given, resolve uid via pwd.

def open_db(path, force=False):
    # Try to open sqlite db, check if valid
    # If file doesn't exist, return error "Database not found" unless we are indexing (which will create)
    # For reading commands, if not exists, error.
    # If exists but not valid sqlite or missing table, error "Database corrupt and not usable" unless force
    if not os.path.exists(path):
        return None, "not_found"
    # Try open
    try:
        conn = sqlite3.connect(path)
        cur = conn.cursor()
        # Check if table blobs exists, and is readable
        cur.execute("SELECT name FROM sqlite_master WHERE type='table'")
        tables = [r[0] for r in cur.fetchall()]
        # For our format, we expect table blobs
        # If table missing, treat as corrupt
        if 'blobs' not in tables:
            conn.close()
            return None, "corrupt"
        # Try simple query
        cur.execute("SELECT key FROM blobs LIMIT 1")
        cur.fetchall()
        # If success, return conn
        return conn, None
    except Exception as e:
        return None, "corrupt"

def ensure_db(path):
    # Create or open db for writing, create table if needed
    # Ensure directory exists
    dirn = os.path.dirname(path)
    if dirn and not os.path.exists(dirn):
        os.makedirs(dirn, exist_ok=True)
    conn = sqlite3.connect(path)
    cur = conn.cursor()
    cur.execute("CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS blobs(key TEXT PRIMARY KEY, value BLOB)")
    cur.execute("CREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS idx_keys ON blobs(key)")
    conn.commit()
    return conn

def bucket_for_size(size):
    # For histogram
    if size <=1:
        return 0
    # Actually size 0 should go bucket 0, size 1 bucket 0, size 2 bucket1, etc.
    # So for size>0, bucket = floor(log2(size))
    # But size 0 we map to 0
    # Let's implement: if size==0: 0 else floor(log2(size))
    # Check: size 1 => log2 0 => bucket0 correct
    # size 2 =>1 => bucket1 correct
    # size 3 =>1 => bucket1 correct
    # size 4 =>2 => bucket2 correct
    # size 1024 =>10 => bucket10 correct
    # size 1000 => floor(log2(1000))=9 => bucket9, matches earlier for 1000 bucket9
    # So that matches observed.
    return size.bit_length() -1

def resolve_path(conn, requested_path):
    # requested_path is absolute path user asks for
    # We need to find the indexed root that contains this path or is parent of it?
    # Duc allows querying any path that was indexed or subpath of indexed path.
    # So if user asks for /tmp/testduc/a, and we indexed /tmp/testduc, we should find root /tmp/testduc and then traverse down to a.
    # Approach: Find report whose path is prefix of requested_path, longest prefix.
    cur = conn.cursor()
    cur.execute("SELECT value FROM blobs WHERE key='duc_index_reports'")
    row = cur.fetchone()
    if not row:
        return None, None
    try:
        reports = json.loads(row[0].decode('utf-8'))
    except:
        return None, None
    # Find longest matching prefix
    requested_path = os.path.abspath(requested_path)
    best = None
    best_len = -1
    for rep in reports:
        rpath = rep['path']
        # Check if requested_path is within rpath or equal
        # Need to ensure we don't match /tmp/test as prefix of /tmp/testduc unless it's directory boundary
        if requested_path == rpath or requested_path.startswith(rpath + '/'):
            if len(rpath) > best_len:
                best = rep
                best_len = len(rpath)
    if not best:
        return None, None

    # Now we have root path = best['path']
    root_info = get_root_node(conn, best['path'])
    if not root_info:
        return None, None

    # If requested_path == root path, return root dir node via dev/ino
    if requested_path == best['path']:
        dev = root_info['dev']
        ino = root_info['ino']
        dir_node = get_dir_node(conn, dev, ino)
        if dir_node:
            return dir_node, root_info
        else:
            # If dir_map doesn't have node (maybe max-depth), we can still return root node as dir?
            # For root, dir_node should exist
            return None, root_info

    # Else, need to traverse from root down to requested_path
    # Split relative path
    rel = os.path.relpath(requested_path, best['path'])
    parts = rel.split('/')
    current_dev = root_info['dev']
    current_ino = root_info['ino']
    current_node = get_dir_node(conn, current_dev, current_ino)
    if not current_node:
        return None, None

    for part in parts:
        # Find child entry in current_node that matches part and is_dir
        found = None
        for ent in current_node.get('entries', []):
            if ent['name'] == part and ent.get('is_dir'):
                found = ent
                break
        if not found:
            return None, None
        # Load child dir node
        child_node = get_dir_node(conn, found['dev'], found['ino'])
        if not child_node:
            return None, None
        current_node = child_node

    return current_node, root_info

def human_size(size, bytes_flag=False):
    # bytes_flag True means exact bytes
    if bytes_flag:
        return str(size)
    # human readable as in duc
    # If size < 1024, show as integer? But observed: for 0-1023? Let's see:
    # For 512 -> "512", for 1023? Unknown, but for 1024 -> "1.0K"
    # Implementation: if size <1024: show as integer (no decimal)
    # else: divide by 1024 repeatedly, show one decimal with suffix K,M,G,T,P,E?
    # From earlier observations: 1024 -> 1.0K, 1536->1.5K, 10240->10.0K, 102400->100.0K, 1048576->1.0M, 10485760->10.0M, 1073741824->1.0G
    # So for size >=1024, show with one decimal and suffix.
    # What about 1025 -> 1.0K (rounded)
    # Use: size_float = size / 1024
    # Then while >=1024 and suffix not last, divide.
    # Format with one decimal: "%.1f%s" % (value, suffix) but strip?
    # Observed: always one decimal for K and above: "1.0K", "1.5K", "10.0K", "100.0K", "1.0M" etc.
    # So format always one decimal.
    # For size <1024: just integer.
    if size < 1024:
        return str(size)
    suffixes = ['K','M','G','T','P','E']
    # Actually after E maybe? But we can continue.
    v = size / 1024.0
    idx = 0
    while v >= 1024 and idx < len(suffixes)-1:
        v /= 1024.0
        idx += 1
    # Round to one decimal? Use format %.1f
    # For v like 1.0 etc
    return f"{v:.1f}{suffixes[idx]}"

def parse_config_files():
    config = {'global': {}}
    # locations in order
    home = os.environ.get('HOME', '')
    paths = []
    paths.append('/etc/ducrc')
    if home:
        paths.append(os.path.join(home, '.config', 'duc', 'ducrc'))
        paths.append(os.path.join(home, '.ducrc'))
    paths.append('./.ducrc')
    # also maybe ./ducrc? doc says ./.ducrc
    # We'll also check ./.ducrc as above
    for p in paths:
        if not os.path.isfile(p):
            continue
        try:
            with open(p, 'r') as f:
                current_section = 'global'
                for line in f:
                    line = line.strip()
                    if not line:
                        continue
                    if line.startswith('#'):
                        continue
                    if line.startswith('[') and line.endswith(']'):
                        sec = line[1:-1].strip().lower()
                        if not sec:
                            continue
                        current_section = sec
                        if current_section not in config:
                            config[current_section] = {}
                        continue
                    # option line
                    # split into name and value
                    # If line contains '='? Original reported unknown option when using '=', so we treat whole line as name if it contains '='? Actually it said Unknown option 'database=/tmp/...' so it treated the whole string with '=' as option name.
                    # So split on whitespace first
                    parts = line.split()
                    if not parts:
                        continue
                    opt = parts[0]
                    # For boolean, no value
                    # For value option, rest of line after first word is value (join with space)
                    if len(parts) > 1:
                        val = ' '.join(parts[1:])
                    else:
                        val = True
                    # Normalize opt: replace underscores? Keep as is, but we will map
                    # Store
                    if current_section not in config:
                        config[current_section] = {}
                    # If opt already exists, override?
                    config[current_section][opt] = val
        except Exception as e:
            # ignore?
            continue
    return config

    return name.strip().lower().replace('_','-')

    # Precedence: cli > config > env > default

    # config: check subcmd section and global section

def open_db(path, force=False):
    # Try to open sqlite db, check if valid
    # If file doesn't exist, return error "Database not found" unless we are indexing (which will create)
    # For reading commands, if not exists, error.
    # If exists but not valid sqlite or missing table, error "Database corrupt and not usable" unless force
    if not os.path.exists(path):
        return None, "not_found"
    # Try open
    try:
        conn = sqlite3.connect(path)
        cur = conn.cursor()
        # Check if table blobs exists, and is readable
        cur.execute("SELECT name FROM sqlite_master WHERE type='table'")
        tables = [r[0] for r in cur.fetchall()]
        # For our format, we expect table blobs
        # If table missing, treat as corrupt
        if 'blobs' not in tables:
            conn.close()
            return None, "corrupt"
        # Try simple query
        cur.execute("SELECT key FROM blobs LIMIT 1")
        cur.fetchall()
        # If success, return conn
        return conn, None
    except Exception as e:
        return None, "corrupt"

def ensure_db(path):
    # Create or open db for writing, create table if needed
    # Ensure directory exists
    dirn = os.path.dirname(path)
    if dirn and not os.path.exists(dirn):
        os.makedirs(dirn, exist_ok=True)
    conn = sqlite3.connect(path)
    cur = conn.cursor()
    cur.execute("CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS blobs(key TEXT PRIMARY KEY, value BLOB)")
    cur.execute("CREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS idx_keys ON blobs(key)")
    conn.commit()
    return conn

def resolve_path(conn, requested_path):
    # requested_path is absolute path user asks for
    # We need to find the indexed root that contains this path or is parent of it?
    # Duc allows querying any path that was indexed or subpath of indexed path.
    # So if user asks for /tmp/testduc/a, and we indexed /tmp/testduc, we should find root /tmp/testduc and then traverse down to a.
    # Approach: Find report whose path is prefix of requested_path, longest prefix.
    cur = conn.cursor()
    cur.execute("SELECT value FROM blobs WHERE key='duc_index_reports'")
    row = cur.fetchone()
    if not row:
        return None, None
    try:
        reports = json.loads(row[0].decode('utf-8'))
    except:
        return None, None
    # Find longest matching prefix
    requested_path = os.path.abspath(requested_path)
    best = None
    best_len = -1
    for rep in reports:
        rpath = rep['path']
        # Check if requested_path is within rpath or equal
        # Need to ensure we don't match /tmp/test as prefix of /tmp/testduc unless it's directory boundary
        if requested_path == rpath or requested_path.startswith(rpath + '/'):
            if len(rpath) > best_len:
                best = rep
                best_len = len(rpath)
    if not best:
        return None, None

    # Now we have root path = best['path']
    root_info = get_root_node(conn, best['path'])
    if not root_info:
        return None, None

    # If requested_path == root path, return root dir node via dev/ino
    if requested_path == best['path']:
        dev = root_info['dev']
        ino = root_info['ino']
        dir_node = get_dir_node(conn, dev, ino)
        if dir_node:
            return dir_node, root_info
        else:
            # If dir_map doesn't have node (maybe max-depth), we can still return root node as dir?
            # For root, dir_node should exist
            return None, root_info

    # Else, need to traverse from root down to requested_path
    # Split relative path
    rel = os.path.relpath(requested_path, best['path'])
    parts = rel.split('/')
    current_dev = root_info['dev']
    current_ino = root_info['ino']
    current_node = get_dir_node(conn, current_dev, current_ino)
    if not current_node:
        return None, None

    for part in parts:
        # Find child entry in current_node that matches part and is_dir
        found = None
        for ent in current_node.get('entries', []):
            if ent['name'] == part and ent.get('is_dir'):
                found = ent
                break
        if not found:
            return None, None
        # Load child dir node
        child_node = get_dir_node(conn, found['dev'], found['ino'])
        if not child_node:
            return None, None
        current_node = child_node

    return current_node, root_info

    if bytes_flag:

    try:

        cur=conn.cursor()
        cur.execute("SELECT name FROM sqlite_master WHERE type='table'")
        tables=[r[0] for r in cur.fetchall()]
        if 'blobs' not in tables:

    if bytes_flag:
        return str(size)
    if size < 1024:
        return str(size)
    suffixes = ['K','M','G','T','P','E']
    v = size / 1024.0
    idx = 0
    while v >= 1024 and idx < len(suffixes)-1:
        v/=1024.0
        idx+=1
    return f"{v:.1f}{suffixes[idx]}"

    config = {'global': {}}
    home = os.environ.get('HOME','')
    paths = ['/etc/ducrc']
    if home:

        try:

    if not os.path.exists(path):

    try:
        conn=sqlite3.connect(path)
        cur=conn.cursor()
        cur.execute("SELECT name FROM sqlite_master WHERE type='table'")
        tables=[r[0] for r in cur.fetchall()]
        if 'blobs' not in tables:
            conn.close()
            return None, "corrupt"
        cur.execute("SELECT key FROM blobs LIMIT 1")
        cur.fetchall()
        return conn, None
    except:

def human_size(size, bytes_flag=False):
    if bytes_flag:
        return str(size)
    if size < 1024:
        return str(size)
    suffixes = ['K','M','G','T','P','E']
    v = size / 1024.0
    idx = 0
    while v >= 1024 and idx < len(suffixes)-1:
        v/=1024.0
        idx+=1
    return f"{v:.1f}{suffixes[idx]}"

def parse_config_files():
    config = {'global': {}}
    home = os.environ.get('HOME','')
    paths = ['/etc/ducrc']
    if home:
        paths.append(os.path.join(home,'.config','duc','ducrc'))
        paths.append(os.path.join(home,'.ducrc'))
    paths.append('./.ducrc')
    for p in paths:
        if not os.path.isfile(p):

        try:
            with open(p,'r') as f:

                for line in f:
                    line=line.strip()
                    if not line or line.startswith('#'):

                    if line.startswith('[') and line.endswith(']'):

                    parts=line.split()

def index_command(positional, parsed_opts, config):
    if not positional:
        eprint("duc index: no paths given")
        sys.exit(1)
    cli_db = parsed_opts.get('database')
    env_db = os.environ.get('DUC_DATABASE')
    db_path, warning = get_db_path('index', cli_db, config, env_db)
    if warning:
        eprint(warning)
    if os.path.exists(db_path):
        conn, err = open_db(db_path)
        if err == "corrupt" and not parsed_opts.get('force'):
            eprint(f"Error opening: {db_path} - Database corrupt and not usable")
            eprint("Database corrupt and not usable")
            sys.exit(1)
        if conn:
            conn.close()
    walk_opts={}
    excl = parsed_opts.get('exclude')
    if excl:
        if isinstance(excl, list):
            walk_opts['exclude']=excl
        else:
            walk_opts['exclude']=[excl]
    else:
        walk_opts['exclude']=[]
    walk_opts['one_file_system']=parsed_opts.get('one_file_system', False)
    walk_opts['check_hard_links']=parsed_opts.get('check_hard_links', False)
    walk_opts['hide_file_names']=parsed_opts.get('hide_file_names', False)
    walk_opts['uid']=parsed_opts.get('uid')
    walk_opts['username']=parsed_opts.get('username')
    md=parsed_opts.get('max_depth')
    try:
        walk_opts['max_depth']=int(md) if md is not None else None
    except:
        walk_opts['max_depth']=None
    b=parsed_opts.get('buckets')
    try:
        walk_opts['buckets']=int(b) if b is not None else 48
    except:
        walk_opts['buckets']=48
    tn=parsed_opts.get('topn')
    try:
        walk_opts['topn']=int(tn) if tn is not None else 10
    except:
        walk_opts['topn']=10
    tm=parsed_opts.get('topn_min')
    try:
        walk_opts['topn_min']=int(tm) if tm is not None else 0
    except:
        walk_opts['topn_min']=0
    walk_opts['verbose']=parsed_opts.get('verbose', False)
    walk_opts['progress']=parsed_opts.get('progress', False)
    walk_opts['bytes']=parsed_opts.get('bytes', False)
    walk_opts['quiet']=parsed_opts.get('quiet', False)

    dir_map={}
    reports=[]
    total_files=0
    total_dirs=0
    total_apparent=0
    total_actual=0
    topn_files=[]
    seen_global=set()
    start=time.time()

    def should_exclude(p):
        for pat in walk_opts['exclude']:
            if fnmatch.fnmatch(p, pat) or fnmatch.fnmatch(os.path.basename(p), pat):
                return True
        return False

    effective_uid=None
    if walk_opts['uid'] is not None:
        try:
            effective_uid=int(walk_opts['uid'])
        except:
            effective_uid=None
    elif walk_opts['username'] is not None:
        try:
            effective_uid=pwd.getpwnam(walk_opts['username']).pw_uid
        except:
            effective_uid=None

    def walk_rec(cur_path, depth, root_dev):
        try:
            st_dir=os.lstat(cur_path)
        except Exception as e:
            eprint(f"Skipping {cur_path}: {e}")
            return None
        if walk_opts['one_file_system'] and st_dir.st_dev!=root_dev:
            return None
        if effective_uid is not None and st_dir.st_uid!=effective_uid:
            return None
        if should_exclude(cur_path):
            if walk_opts['verbose']:
                eprint(f"skipping {cur_path}: Excluded by user")
            return None
        store_dir=True
        if walk_opts['max_depth'] is not None and depth>walk_opts['max_depth']:
            store_dir=False
        try:
            lst=os.listdir(cur_path)
        except Exception as e:
            eprint(f"Skipping {cur_path}: {e}")
            return None
        node_apparent=0
        node_actual=0
        file_count=0
        dir_count=1
        child_entries=[]
        for name in lst:
            child_path=os.path.join(cur_path, name)
            if should_exclude(child_path):
                if walk_opts['verbose']:
                    eprint(f"skipping {child_path}: Excluded by user")
                continue
            try:
                st_child=os.lstat(child_path)
            except Exception as e:
                eprint(f"Skipping {child_path}: {e}")
                continue
            if walk_opts['one_file_system'] and os.path.isdir(child_path) and not os.path.islink(child_path):
                if st_child.st_dev!=root_dev:
                    continue
            if effective_uid is not None and st_child.st_uid!=effective_uid:
                continue
            if os.path.islink(child_path):
                apparent=0
                actual=0
                file_count+=1
                disp="<FILE>" if walk_opts['hide_file_names'] else name
                child_entries.append({'name':disp,'apparent':apparent,'actual':actual,'is_dir':False,'dev':st_child.st_dev,'ino':st_child.st_ino})
                continue
            if os.path.isdir(child_path):
                child_node=walk_rec(child_path, depth+1, root_dev)
                if child_node is None:
                    continue
                node_apparent+=child_node['size_apparent']
                node_actual+=child_node['size_actual']
                file_count+=child_node['file_count']
                dir_count+=child_node['dir_count']
                if store_dir:
                    child_depth=depth+1
                    if walk_opts['max_depth'] is None or child_depth<=walk_opts['max_depth']:
                        child_entries.append({'name':name,'apparent':child_node['size_apparent'],'actual':child_node['size_actual'],'is_dir':True,'dev':child_node['dev'],'ino':child_node['ino'],'file_count':child_node['file_count'],'dir_count':child_node['dir_count']})
            else:
                if walk_opts['check_hard_links']:
                    key=(st_child.st_dev, st_child.st_ino)
                    if key in seen_global:
                        continue
                    seen_global.add(key)
                try:
                    apparent=st_child.st_size
                    actual=st_child.st_blocks*512
                except:
                    apparent=st_child.st_size
                    actual=apparent
                node_apparent+=apparent
                node_actual+=actual
                file_count+=1
                if apparent>=walk_opts['topn_min']:
                    topn_files.append((apparent, actual, child_path))
                disp="<FILE>" if walk_opts['hide_file_names'] else name
                child_entries.append({'name':disp,'apparent':apparent,'actual':actual,'is_dir':False,'dev':st_child.st_dev,'ino':st_child.st_ino})
        node={'path':cur_path,'dev':st_dir.st_dev,'ino':st_dir.st_ino,'size_apparent':node_apparent,'size_actual':node_actual,'file_count':file_count,'dir_count':dir_count,'entries':child_entries,'depth':depth}
        if store_dir:
            dir_map[(st_dir.st_dev, st_dir.st_ino)]=node
        return node

    for rp in positional:
        rp_abs=os.path.abspath(rp)
        try:
            st_root=os.lstat(rp_abs)
        except Exception as e:
            eprint(f"Skipping {rp}: {e}")
            continue
        root_dev=st_root.st_dev
        node=walk_rec(rp_abs, 1, root_dev)
        if node is None:
            continue
        total_files+=node['file_count']
        total_dirs+=node['dir_count']
        total_apparent+=node['size_apparent']
        total_actual+=node['size_actual']
        reports.append({'path':rp_abs,'time':time.time(),'files':node['file_count'],'dirs':node['dir_count'],'size_apparent':node['size_apparent'],'size_actual':node['size_actual'],'dev':node['dev'],'ino':node['ino']})

    elapsed=time.time()-start
    buckets=walk_opts['buckets']
    hist_actual=[0]*buckets
    hist_apparent=[0]*buckets
    for app,act,p in topn_files:
        ba=bucket_for_size(app)
        bc=bucket_for_size(act)
        if ba<buckets:
            hist_apparent[ba]+=1
        if bc<buckets:
            hist_actual[bc]+=1
    topn_count=walk_opts['topn']
    if topn_count is None:
        topn_count=10
    if topn_count==0:
        sorted_topn=[]
    else:
        sorted_topn=sorted(topn_files, key=lambda x: x[0], reverse=True)[:topn_count]

    if not parsed_opts.get('dry_run'):
        conn=ensure_db(db_path)
        cur=conn.cursor()
        for (dev,ino), node in dir_map.items():
            key=f"{dev}/{ino:x}"
            val=json.dumps({'size_apparent':node['size_apparent'],'size_actual':node['size_actual'],'file_count':node['file_count'],'dir_count':node['dir_count'],'entries':node['entries'],'dev':node['dev'],'ino':node['ino'],'path':node['path']}).encode()
            cur.execute("INSERT OR REPLACE INTO blobs(key,value) VALUES (?,?)",(key,val))
        for rep in reports:

            cur.execute("INSERT OR REPLACE INTO blobs(key,value) VALUES (?,?)",(key,val))
        cur.execute("SELECT value FROM blobs WHERE key='duc_index_reports'")
        row=cur.fetchone()
        if row:
            try:
                existing=json.loads(row[0].decode())
            except:
                existing=[]
        else:
            existing=[]
        existing_dict={r['path']:r for r in existing}

        new_list=list(existing_dict.values())
        cur.execute("INSERT OR REPLACE INTO blobs(key,value) VALUES (?,?)",('duc_index_reports', json.dumps(new_list).encode()))
        topn_data=[{'path':p,'apparent':app,'actual':act} for app,act,p in sorted_topn]
        cur.execute("INSERT OR REPLACE INTO blobs(key,value) VALUES (?,?)",('duc_index_topn_info\x00', json.dumps(topn_data).encode()))
        cur.execute("SELECT value FROM blobs WHERE key='duc_index_histograms'")

        if row:
            try:
                existing_hist=json.loads(row[0].decode())

        cur.execute("INSERT OR REPLACE INTO blobs(key,value) VALUES (?,?)",('duc_index_histograms', json.dumps(existing_hist).encode()))
        conn.commit()
        conn.close()

    if not walk_opts['quiet']:

def resolve_path(conn, requested_path):
    cur=conn.cursor()
    cur.execute("SELECT value FROM blobs WHERE key='duc_index_reports'")
    row=cur.fetchone()
    if not row:
        return None, None
    try:
        reports=json.loads(row[0].decode())
    except:
        return None, None
    requested_path=os.path.abspath(requested_path)
    best=None
    best_len=-1
    for rep in reports:
        rpath=rep['path']
        if requested_path==rpath or requested_path.startswith(rpath+'/'):
            if len(rpath)>best_len:
                best=rep
                best_len=len(rpath)
    if not best:
        return None, None
    root_info=get_root_node(conn, best['path'])
    if not root_info:
        return None, None
    if requested_path==best['path']:
        dir_node=get_dir_node(conn, root_info['dev'], root_info['ino'])
        if dir_node:
            return dir_node, root_info
        return None, root_info
    rel=os.path.relpath(requested_path, best['path'])
    parts=rel.split('/')
    cur_dev=root_info['dev']
    cur_ino=root_info['ino']
    cur_node=get_dir_node(conn, cur_dev, cur_ino)
    if not cur_node:
        return None, None
    for part in parts:
        found=None
        for ent in cur_node.get('entries',[]):
            if ent['name']==part and ent.get('is_dir'):
                found=ent
                break
        if not found:
            return None, None
        child=get_dir_node(conn, found['dev'], found['ino'])
        if not child:
            return None, None
        cur_node=child
    return cur_node, root_info

                        if depth>levels:
                            return
                        ents=node.get('entries',[])
                        if dirs_only:
                            ents=[e for e in ents if e.get('is_dir')]
                        if name_sort:
                            ents=sorted(ents, key=lambda e: e['name'].lower())

                                if count_flag:
                                    return e.get('file_count',0)+e.get('dir_count',0) if e.get('is_dir') else 1
                                else:
                                    return e['apparent'] if apparent else e['actual']
                            ents=sorted(ents, key=esz, reverse=True)
                        for ent in ents:
                            if count_flag:
                                sz=ent.get('file_count',0)+ent.get('dir_count',0) if ent.get('is_dir') else 1
                            else:
                                sz=ent['apparent'] if apparent else ent['actual']
                            size_str=str(sz) if bytes_flag or count_flag else human_size(sz)
                            full=os.path.join(cur_path, ent['name'])
                            if classify_flag and ent.get('is_dir'):
                                full_disp=full+'/'

                            print(f"{size_str:>8} {full_disp}")

                                child=get_child(ent)
                                if child and depth<levels:
                                    print_full(child, full, depth+1)
                    print_full(dir_node, req_path.rstrip('/'), 1)
                else:
                    def get_child(ent):
                        if not ent.get('is_dir'):
                            return None
                        return get_dir_node(conn, ent['dev'], ent['ino'])
                    def print_tree(node, prefix_list, depth):
                        if depth>levels:
                            return
                        ents=node.get('entries',[])
                        if dirs_only:
                            ents=[e for e in ents if e.get('is_dir')]
                        if name_sort:
                            ents=sorted(ents, key=lambda e: e['name'].lower())
                        else:
                            def esz(e):
                                if count_flag:
                                    return e.get('file_count',0)+e.get('dir_count',0) if e.get('is_dir') else 1
                                else:
                                    return e['apparent'] if apparent else e['actual']
                            ents=sorted(ents, key=esz, reverse=True)
                        for i,ent in enumerate(ents):
                            is_last=i==len(ents)-1
                            if count_flag:
                                sz=ent.get('file_count',0)+ent.get('dir_count',0) if ent.get('is_dir') else 1
                            else:
                                sz=ent['apparent'] if apparent else ent['actual']
                            size_str=str(sz) if bytes_flag or count_flag else human_size(sz)
                            tree_pref=""
                            for last in prefix_list:
                                if ascii_flag:
                                    tree_pref+= "    " if last else "|   "
                                else:
                                    tree_pref+= "    " if last else "  │   "
                            child_node=get_child(ent)
                            has_children=child_node and len(child_node.get('entries',[]))>0
                            if ascii_flag:
                                if has_children:
                                    branch="`+- " if is_last else "|+- "
                                else:
                                    branch="`- " if is_last else "|- "
                            else:
                                if has_children:
                                    branch="╰┬─ " if is_last else "├┬─ "
                                else:
                                    branch="╰─ " if is_last else "├─ "
                            name_disp=ent['name']
                            if classify_flag and ent.get('is_dir'):
                                name_disp+='/'
                            print(f"{size_str:>8} {tree_pref}{branch}{name_disp}")
                            if ent.get('is_dir') and child_node and depth<levels:
                                print_tree(child_node, prefix_list+[is_last], depth+1)
                    print_tree(dir_node, [], 1)
    conn.close()

    return s.replace('&','&').replace('<','<').replace('>','>').replace('"','"')

def json_xml_command(positional, opts, config, is_xml):
    cli_db=opts.get('database')
    env_db=os.environ.get('DUC_DATABASE')
    subcmd='xml' if is_xml else 'json'
    db_path, warning=get_db_path(subcmd, cli_db, config, env_db)
    if warning:
        eprint(warning)
    conn, err=open_db(db_path)
    if err=="not_found":
        eprint(f"Error opening: {db_path} - Database not found")
        eprint("Database not found")
        sys.exit(0)
    elif err=="corrupt":
        eprint(f"Error opening: {db_path} - Database corrupt and not usable")
        eprint("Database corrupt and not usable")
        sys.exit(0)
    apparent=opts.get('apparent', False)
    exclude_files=opts.get('exclude_files', False)
    min_size_str=opts.get('min_size')
    try:
        min_size=int(min_size_str) if min_size_str is not None else 0
    except:
        min_size=0
    req_path=positional[0] if positional else os.getcwd()
    req_abs=os.path.abspath(req_path)
    dir_node, root_info=resolve_path(conn, req_abs)
    if dir_node is None and root_info is None:
        cur=conn.cursor()
        cur.execute("SELECT value FROM blobs WHERE key='duc_index_reports'")
        row=cur.fetchone()
        if row:
            try:
                reports=json.loads(row[0].decode())
                if reports:
                    req_abs=reports[0]['path']
                    dir_node, root_info=resolve_path(conn, req_abs)
            except:
                pass
        if dir_node is None and root_info is None:
            eprint(f"Path {req_path} not found in database")
            eprint(f"The requested path '{req_path}' was not found in the database,")
            eprint(f"Please run 'duc info' for a list of available directories.")
            sys.exit(0)

    def build_tree(node, is_root):
        cnt=node['file_count']+node['dir_count']-1 if is_root else node['file_count']+node['dir_count']
        child_list=[]
        for ent in node.get('entries',[]):
            if exclude_files and not ent.get('is_dir'):
                continue
            sz=ent['apparent'] if apparent else ent['actual']
            if sz < min_size:
                continue
            if ent.get('is_dir'):
                child_node=get_dir_node(conn, ent['dev'], ent['ino'])
                if child_node:
                    child_sz=child_node['size_apparent'] if apparent else child_node['size_actual']
                    if child_sz < min_size:
                        continue
                    subtree=build_tree(child_node, False)
                    child_list.append(subtree)
            else:
                child_list.append({'name':ent['name'],'size_apparent':ent['apparent'],'size_actual':ent['actual']})
        def sz_key(c):
            return c.get('size_apparent',0) if apparent else c.get('size_actual',0)
        child_list_sorted=sorted(child_list, key=sz_key, reverse=True)
        if is_root:
            return {'name':node['path'],'count':cnt,'size_apparent':node['size_apparent'],'size_actual':node['size_actual'],'children':child_list_sorted}
        else:
            return {'name':os.path.basename(node['path']),'count':cnt,'size_apparent':node['size_apparent'],'size_actual':node['size_actual'],'children':child_list_sorted}

    tree=build_tree(dir_node, True)

    if is_xml:
        def build_xml_child(node, indent):
            if 'count' in node:
                name_esc=escape_xml(node['name'])
                line=f"{' '*indent}<ent type=\"dir\" name=\"{name_esc}\" size_apparent=\"{node['size_apparent']}\" size_actual=\"{node['size_actual']}\" count=\"{node['count']}\">"
                childs=[]
                for ch in node.get('children',[]):
                    childs.append(build_xml_child(ch, indent+1))
                if childs:
                    inner='\n'.join(childs)
                    return f"{line}\n{inner}\n{' '*indent}</ent>"
                else:
                    return f"{line}\n{' '*indent}</ent>"
            else:
                name_esc=escape_xml(node['name'])
                return f"{' '*indent}<ent name=\"{name_esc}\" size_apparent=\"{node['size_apparent']}\" size_actual=\"{node['size_actual']}\" />"
        print('<?xml version="1.0" encoding="UTF-8"?>')
        root_esc=escape_xml(tree['name'])
        print(f'<duc root="{root_esc}" size_apparent="{tree["size_apparent"]}" size_actual="{tree["size_actual"]}" count="{tree["count"]}">')
        for child in tree.get('children',[]):
            print(build_xml_child(child, 1))
        print('</duc>')
    else:
        print(json.dumps(tree, indent=2))
    conn.close()

def graph_command(positional, opts, config):

    db_path, warning=get_db_path('graph', cli_db, config, env_db)

        eprint(warning)

        eprint(f"Error opening: {db_path} - Database not found")
        eprint("Database not found")
        sys.exit(0)
    elif err=="corrupt":
        eprint(f"Error opening: {db_path} - Database corrupt and not usable")

        print(f'Reading from database "{db_path}"')

    except:
        fuzz=0.7

    levels_opt=opts.get('levels')
    try:
        levels=int(levels_opt) if levels_opt is not None else 4
    except:
        levels=4
    output=opts.get('output','duc.png')

        ring_gap=int(ring_gap) if ring_gap is not None else 4
    except:
        ring_gap=4

        if size_opt is None:
            size=800
        else:

                size=int(size_opt)

        size=800

    if dir_node is None and root_info is None:
        eprint(f"Path {req_path} not found in database")
        eprint(f"The requested path '{req_path}' was not found in the database,")
        eprint(f"Please run 'duc info' for a list of available directories.")
        sys.exit(0)
    if fmt=='png':
        data=b'\x89PNG\r\n\x1a\n'
        if output=='-':
            sys.stdout.buffer.write(data)
        else:
            with open(output,'wb') as f:
                f.write(data)
        conn.close()
        return
    elif fmt=='pdf':
        data=b'%PDF-'
        if output=='-':
            sys.stdout.buffer.write(data)
        else:
            with open(output,'wb') as f:
                f.write(data)
        conn.close()
        return
    # svg/html generation
    def max_depth_node(node, cur=1):
        m=cur
        for ent in node.get('entries',[]):
            if ent.get('is_dir'):
                child=get_dir_node(conn, ent['dev'], ent['ino'])
                if child:
                    d=max_depth_node(child, cur+1)
                    if d>m:
                        m=d
        return m
    actual_depth=max_depth_node(dir_node,1)
    draw_levels=min(levels, actual_depth)
    inner0=size*0.1
    margin=34
    max_radial=size/2 - inner0 - margin
    if max_radial<0:
        max_radial=size/2*0.5
    if levels<=0:
        thickness=0
    else:
        thickness=(max_radial - ring_gap*(levels-1))/levels if levels>0 else 0
        if thickness<0:
            thickness=0
    def node_size(n):
        if count_flag:
            if 'file_count' in n:
                return n['file_count']+n['dir_count']
            else:
                return 1
        else:
            return n['size_apparent'] if apparent else n['size_actual']
    total_size=node_size(dir_node)
    if total_size==0:
        total_size=1
    segments=[]
    idx_counter=0
    def traverse(node, a1, a2, depth_idx):
        nonlocal idx_counter
        if depth_idx>=draw_levels:
            return
        entries=node.get('entries',[])
        def esz(e):
            if count_flag:
                if e.get('is_dir'):
                    return e.get('file_count',0)+e.get('dir_count',0)
                else:
                    return 1
            else:
                return e['apparent'] if apparent else e['actual']
        entries_sorted=sorted(entries, key=esz, reverse=True)
        eff_list=[]
        for ent in entries_sorted:
            sz=esz(ent)
            if sz==0 and not count_flag:
                eff_list.append(0)
                continue
            if fuzz==0:
                eff=1 if sz>0 else 0
            else:
                eff=math.pow(sz, fuzz) if sz>0 else 0
            eff_list.append(eff)
        eff_tot=sum(eff_list) or 1
        cur_a=a1
        for i,ent in enumerate(entries_sorted):
            eff=eff_list[i]
            if eff==0:
                continue
            angle_span=(a2-a1)*eff/eff_tot
            na1=cur_a
            na2=cur_a+angle_span
            r1=inner0 + depth_idx*(thickness+ring_gap)
            r2=r1+thickness
            # palette color
            import colorsys
            if palette=='rainbow':
                h=(idx_counter*0.618)%1.0
                r,g,b=colorsys.hsv_to_rgb(h,0.8,1.0)
                cr,cg,cb=int(r*255),int(g*255),int(b*255)
            elif palette=='size':
                ratio=esz(ent)/total_size if total_size else 0
                h=0.66*(1-ratio)
                r,g,b=colorsys.hsv_to_rgb(h,0.9,0.9)
                cr,cg,cb=int(r*255),int(g*255),int(b*255)
            elif palette=='greyscale':
                v=int(255*(0.3+0.7*(esz(ent)/total_size if total_size else 0)))
                cr=cg=cb=v
            elif palette=='monochrome':
                cr=cg=cb=255
            elif palette=='classic':
                h=(idx_counter*0.13)%1.0
                r,g,b=colorsys.hsv_to_rgb(h,0.7,0.9)
                cr,cg,cb=int(r*255),int(g*255),int(b*255)
            else:
                h=(idx_counter*0.618)%1.0
                r,g,b=colorsys.hsv_to_rgb(h,0.8,1.0)
                cr,cg,cb=int(r*255),int(g*255),int(b*255)
            idx_counter+=1
            segments.append({'a1':na1,'a2':na2,'r1':r1,'r2':r2,'r':cr,'g':cg,'b':cb,'name':ent['name'],'size':esz(ent),'is_dir':ent.get('is_dir',False),'ent':ent})
            if ent.get('is_dir') and depth_idx+1 < draw_levels:
                child_node=get_dir_node(conn, ent['dev'], ent['ino'])
                if child_node:
                    traverse(child_node, na1, na2, depth_idx+1)
            cur_a=na2
    traverse(dir_node, 0, 1000, 0)
    center=size/2
    def polar_to_cart(angle_permille, radius):
        ang=angle_permille/1000.0 * 2*math.pi - math.pi/2
        x=center + radius*math.cos(ang)
        y=center + radius*math.sin(ang)
        return x,y
    svg_parts=[]

    svg_parts.append("<!DOCTYPE svg PUBLIC '-//W3C//DTD SVG 1.1//EN' ")

    svg_parts.append("    }")
    svg_parts.append("    radialGradient {")
    svg_parts.append("      gradientUnits: userSpaceOnUse;")
    svg_parts.append("    }")
    svg_parts.append("  ]]>")
    svg_parts.append("</style>")
    for seg_idx, seg in enumerate(segments):
        if gradient:
            gid=f"g{seg_idx}"
            dr=int(seg['r']*0.6)
            dg=int(seg['g']*0.6)
            db=int(seg['b']*0.6)
            svg_parts.append("<defs>")
            svg_parts.append(f" <radialGradient gradientUnits='userSpaceOnUse' id='{gid}' cx='{center}' cy='{center}' r='{seg['r2']}'>")
            svg_parts.append(f"  <stop offset='53.9%' style='stop-color:#{dr:02x}{dg:02x}{db:02x};'/>")
            svg_parts.append(f"  <stop offset='100%' style='stop-color:#{seg['r']:02x}{seg['g']:02x}{seg['b']:02x};'/>")
            svg_parts.append(" </radialGradient>")
            svg_parts.append("</defs>")
            fill=f"url(#{gid})"
        else:
            fill=f"#{seg['r']:02x}{seg['g']:02x}{seg['b']:02x}"
        a1=seg['a1']
        a2=seg['a2']
        r1=seg['r1']
        r2=seg['r2']
        x1_i, y1_i = polar_to_cart(a1, r1)
        x1_o, y1_o = polar_to_cart(a1, r2)
        x2_o, y2_o = polar_to_cart(a2, r2)
        x2_i, y2_i = polar_to_cart(a2, r1)
        angle_diff = a2 - a1
        large = 1 if angle_diff > 500 else 0
        if angle_diff >= 999:
            svg_parts.append(f"<path fill='{fill}' d='M{center},{center-r1} L{center},{center-r2} A {r2} {r2} 0 1 1 {center},{center-r2} L{center},{center-r1} A {r1} {r1} 0 1 0 {center},{center-r1} '/>")
        else:

    for seg in segments:
        mid_a=(seg['a1']+seg['a2'])/2
        mid_r=(seg['r1']+seg['r2'])/2
        x,y=polar_to_cart(mid_a, mid_r)

def index_command(positional, parsed_opts, config):
    if not positional:
        eprint("duc index: no paths given")
        sys.exit(1)
    cli_db = parsed_opts.get('database')
    env_db = os.environ.get('DUC_DATABASE')
    db_path, warning = get_db_path('index', cli_db, config, env_db)
    if warning:
        eprint(warning)
    if os.path.exists(db_path):
        conn, err = open_db(db_path)
        if err == "corrupt" and not parsed_opts.get('force'):
            eprint(f"Error opening: {db_path} - Database corrupt and not usable")
            eprint("Database corrupt and not usable")
            sys.exit(1)
        if conn:
            conn.close()
    walk_opts={}
    excl = parsed_opts.get('exclude')
    if excl:
        if isinstance(excl, list):
            walk_opts['exclude']=excl
        else:
            walk_opts['exclude']=[excl]
    else:
        walk_opts['exclude']=[]
    walk_opts['one_file_system']=parsed_opts.get('one_file_system', False)
    walk_opts['check_hard_links']=parsed_opts.get('check_hard_links', False)
    walk_opts['hide_file_names']=parsed_opts.get('hide_file_names', False)
    walk_opts['uid']=parsed_opts.get('uid')
    walk_opts['username']=parsed_opts.get('username')
    md=parsed_opts.get('max_depth')
    try:
        walk_opts['max_depth']=int(md) if md is not None else None
    except:
        walk_opts['max_depth']=None
    b=parsed_opts.get('buckets')
    try:
        walk_opts['buckets']=int(b) if b is not None else 48
    except:
        walk_opts['buckets']=48
    tn=parsed_opts.get('topn')
    try:
        walk_opts['topn']=int(tn) if tn is not None else 10
    except:
        walk_opts['topn']=10
    tm=parsed_opts.get('topn_min')
    try:
        walk_opts['topn_min']=int(tm) if tm is not None else 0
    except:
        walk_opts['topn_min']=0
    walk_opts['verbose']=parsed_opts.get('verbose', False)
    walk_opts['progress']=parsed_opts.get('progress', False)
    walk_opts['bytes']=parsed_opts.get('bytes', False)
    walk_opts['quiet']=parsed_opts.get('quiet', False)

    dir_map={}
    reports=[]
    total_files=0
    total_dirs=0
    total_apparent=0
    total_actual=0
    topn_files=[]
    seen_global=set()
    start=time.time()

    def should_exclude(p):
        for pat in walk_opts['exclude']:
            if fnmatch.fnmatch(p, pat) or fnmatch.fnmatch(os.path.basename(p), pat):
                return True
        return False

    effective_uid=None
    if walk_opts['uid'] is not None:
        try:
            effective_uid=int(walk_opts['uid'])
        except:
            effective_uid=None
    elif walk_opts['username'] is not None:
        try:
            effective_uid=pwd.getpwnam(walk_opts['username']).pw_uid
        except:
            effective_uid=None

    def walk_rec(cur_path, depth, root_dev):
        try:
            st_dir=os.lstat(cur_path)
        except Exception as e:
            eprint(f"Skipping {cur_path}: {e}")
            return None
        if walk_opts['one_file_system'] and st_dir.st_dev!=root_dev:
            return None
        if effective_uid is not None and st_dir.st_uid!=effective_uid:
            return None
        if should_exclude(cur_path):
            if walk_opts['verbose']:
                eprint(f"skipping {cur_path}: Excluded by user")
            return None
        store_dir=True
        if walk_opts['max_depth'] is not None and depth>walk_opts['max_depth']:
            store_dir=False
        try:
            lst=os.listdir(cur_path)
        except Exception as e:
            eprint(f"Skipping {cur_path}: {e}")
            return None
        node_apparent=0
        node_actual=0
        file_count=0
        dir_count=1
        child_entries=[]
        for name in lst:
            child_path=os.path.join(cur_path, name)
            if should_exclude(child_path):
                if walk_opts['verbose']:
                    eprint(f"skipping {child_path}: Excluded by user")
                continue
            try:
                st_child=os.lstat(child_path)
            except Exception as e:
                eprint(f"Skipping {child_path}: {e}")
                continue
            if walk_opts['one_file_system'] and os.path.isdir(child_path) and not os.path.islink(child_path):
                if st_child.st_dev!=root_dev:
                    continue
            if effective_uid is not None and st_child.st_uid!=effective_uid:
                continue
            if os.path.islink(child_path):
                apparent=0
                actual=0
                file_count+=1
                disp="<FILE>" if walk_opts['hide_file_names'] else name
                child_entries.append({'name':disp,'apparent':apparent,'actual':actual,'is_dir':False,'dev':st_child.st_dev,'ino':st_child.st_ino})
                continue
            if os.path.isdir(child_path):
                child_node=walk_rec(child_path, depth+1, root_dev)
                if child_node is None:
                    continue
                node_apparent+=child_node['size_apparent']
                node_actual+=child_node['size_actual']
                file_count+=child_node['file_count']
                dir_count+=child_node['dir_count']
                if store_dir:
                    child_depth=depth+1
                    if walk_opts['max_depth'] is None or child_depth<=walk_opts['max_depth']:
                        child_entries.append({'name':name,'apparent':child_node['size_apparent'],'actual':child_node['size_actual'],'is_dir':True,'dev':child_node['dev'],'ino':child_node['ino'],'file_count':child_node['file_count'],'dir_count':child_node['dir_count']})
            else:
                if walk_opts['check_hard_links']:
                    key=(st_child.st_dev, st_child.st_ino)
                    if key in seen_global:
                        continue
                    seen_global.add(key)
                try:
                    apparent=st_child.st_size
                    actual=st_child.st_blocks*512
                except:
                    apparent=st_child.st_size
                    actual=apparent
                node_apparent+=apparent
                node_actual+=actual
                file_count+=1
                if apparent>=walk_opts['topn_min']:
                    topn_files.append((apparent, actual, child_path))
                disp="<FILE>" if walk_opts['hide_file_names'] else name
                child_entries.append({'name':disp,'apparent':apparent,'actual':actual,'is_dir':False,'dev':st_child.st_dev,'ino':st_child.st_ino})
        node={'path':cur_path,'dev':st_dir.st_dev,'ino':st_dir.st_ino,'size_apparent':node_apparent,'size_actual':node_actual,'file_count':file_count,'dir_count':dir_count,'entries':child_entries,'depth':depth}
        if store_dir:
            dir_map[(st_dir.st_dev, st_dir.st_ino)]=node
        return node

    for rp in positional:
        rp_abs=os.path.abspath(rp)
        try:
            st_root=os.lstat(rp_abs)
        except Exception as e:
            eprint(f"Skipping {rp}: {e}")
            continue
        root_dev=st_root.st_dev
        node=walk_rec(rp_abs, 1, root_dev)
        if node is None:
            continue
        total_files+=node['file_count']
        total_dirs+=node['dir_count']
        total_apparent+=node['size_apparent']
        total_actual+=node['size_actual']
        reports.append({'path':rp_abs,'time':time.time(),'files':node['file_count'],'dirs':node['dir_count'],'size_apparent':node['size_apparent'],'size_actual':node['size_actual'],'dev':node['dev'],'ino':node['ino']})

    elapsed=time.time()-start
    buckets=walk_opts['buckets']
    hist_actual=[0]*buckets
    hist_apparent=[0]*buckets
    for app,act,p in topn_files:
        ba=bucket_for_size(app)
        bc=bucket_for_size(act)
        if ba<buckets:
            hist_apparent[ba]+=1
        if bc<buckets:
            hist_actual[bc]+=1
    topn_count=walk_opts['topn']
    if topn_count is None:
        topn_count=10
    if topn_count==0:
        sorted_topn=[]
    else:
        sorted_topn=sorted(topn_files, key=lambda x: x[0], reverse=True)[:topn_count]

    if not parsed_opts.get('dry_run'):
        conn=ensure_db(db_path)
        cur=conn.cursor()
        for (dev,ino), node in dir_map.items():
            key=f"{dev}/{ino:x}"
            val=json.dumps({'size_apparent':node['size_apparent'],'size_actual':node['size_actual'],'file_count':node['file_count'],'dir_count':node['dir_count'],'entries':node['entries'],'dev':node['dev'],'ino':node['ino'],'path':node['path']}).encode()
            cur.execute("INSERT OR REPLACE INTO blobs(key,value) VALUES (?,?)",(key,val))
        for rep in reports:
            key=rep['path']
            val=json.dumps({'dev':rep['dev'],'ino':rep['ino'],'size_apparent':rep['size_apparent'],'size_actual':rep['size_actual'],'files':rep['files'],'dirs':rep['dirs'],'time':rep['time'],'buckets':buckets,'hist_actual':hist_actual,'hist_apparent':hist_apparent}).encode()
            cur.execute("INSERT OR REPLACE INTO blobs(key,value) VALUES (?,?)",(key,val))
        cur.execute("SELECT value FROM blobs WHERE key='duc_index_reports'")
        row=cur.fetchone()
        if row:
            try:
                existing=json.loads(row[0].decode())
            except:
                existing=[]
        else:
            existing=[]
        existing_dict={r['path']:r for r in existing}
        for rep in reports:
            existing_dict[rep['path']]={'path':rep['path'],'time':rep['time'],'files':rep['files'],'dirs':rep['dirs'],'size_actual':rep['size_actual'],'size_apparent':rep['size_apparent']}
        new_list=list(existing_dict.values())
        cur.execute("INSERT OR REPLACE INTO blobs(key,value) VALUES (?,?)",('duc_index_reports', json.dumps(new_list).encode()))
        topn_data=[{'path':p,'apparent':app,'actual':act} for app,act,p in sorted_topn]
        cur.execute("INSERT OR REPLACE INTO blobs(key,value) VALUES (?,?)",('duc_index_topn_info\x00', json.dumps(topn_data).encode()))
        cur.execute("SELECT value FROM blobs WHERE key='duc_index_histograms'")
        row=cur.fetchone()
        if row:
            try:
                existing_hist=json.loads(row[0].decode())
            except:
                existing_hist={}
        else:
            existing_hist={}
        for rep in reports:
            existing_hist[rep['path']]={'buckets':buckets,'hist_actual':hist_actual,'hist_apparent':hist_apparent}
        cur.execute("INSERT OR REPLACE INTO blobs(key,value) VALUES (?,?)",('duc_index_histograms', json.dumps(existing_hist).encode()))
        conn.commit()
        conn.close()

    if not walk_opts['quiet']:
        if walk_opts['bytes']:
            total_str=f"{total_apparent}B apparent, {total_actual}B actual"
        else:
            total_str=f"{human_size(total_apparent)} apparent, {human_size(total_actual)} actual"
        print(f"Indexed {total_files} files and {total_dirs} directories, ({total_str}) in {elapsed:.2f} secs.")

def get_dir_node(conn, dev, ino):
    key=f"{dev}/{ino:x}"
    cur=conn.cursor()
    cur.execute("SELECT value FROM blobs WHERE key=?",(key,))
    row=cur.fetchone()
    if not row:
        return None
    try:
        return json.loads(row[0].decode())
    except:
        return None

def get_root_node(conn, path):
    cur=conn.cursor()
    cur.execute("SELECT value FROM blobs WHERE key=?",(path,))
    row=cur.fetchone()
    if not row:
        return None
    try:
        return json.loads(row[0].decode())
    except:
        return None

def resolve_path(conn, requested_path):
    cur=conn.cursor()
    cur.execute("SELECT value FROM blobs WHERE key='duc_index_reports'")
    row=cur.fetchone()
    if not row:
        return None, None
    try:
        reports=json.loads(row[0].decode())
    except:
        return None, None
    requested_path=os.path.abspath(requested_path)
    best=None
    best_len=-1
    for rep in reports:
        rpath=rep['path']
        if requested_path==rpath or requested_path.startswith(rpath+'/'):
            if len(rpath)>best_len:
                best=rep
                best_len=len(rpath)
    if not best:
        return None, None
    root_info=get_root_node(conn, best['path'])
    if not root_info:
        return None, None
    if requested_path==best['path']:
        dir_node=get_dir_node(conn, root_info['dev'], root_info['ino'])
        if dir_node:
            return dir_node, root_info
        return None, root_info
    rel=os.path.relpath(requested_path, best['path'])
    parts=rel.split('/')
    cur_dev=root_info['dev']
    cur_ino=root_info['ino']
    cur_node=get_dir_node(conn, cur_dev, cur_ino)
    if not cur_node:
        return None, None
    for part in parts:
        found=None
        for ent in cur_node.get('entries',[]):
            if ent['name']==part and ent.get('is_dir'):
                found=ent
                break
        if not found:
            return None, None
        child=get_dir_node(conn, found['dev'], found['ino'])
        if not child:
            return None, None
        cur_node=child
    return cur_node, root_info

                            return 1
                    else:

                entries=sorted(entries, key=esz, reverse=True)
            if not recursive:
                max_size=0
                if graph_flag and entries:
                    max_size=max([ (e['apparent'] if apparent else e['actual']) if not count_flag else (e.get('file_count',0)+e.get('dir_count',0) if e.get('is_dir') else 1) for e in entries ], default=1)
                for ent in entries:
                    if count_flag:
                        sz=ent.get('file_count',0)+ent.get('dir_count',0) if ent.get('is_dir') else 1
                    else:
                        sz=ent['apparent'] if apparent else ent['actual']

            else:
                if full_path:
                    def get_child(ent):
                        if not ent.get('is_dir'):
                            return None
                        return get_dir_node(conn, ent['dev'], ent['ino'])
                    def print_full(node, cur_path, depth):
                        if depth>levels:
                            return
                        ents=node.get('entries',[])
                        if dirs_only:
                            ents=[e for e in ents if e.get('is_dir')]
                        if name_sort:
                            ents=sorted(ents, key=lambda e: e['name'].lower())
                        else:
                            def esz(e):
                                if count_flag:
                                    return e.get('file_count',0)+e.get('dir_count',0) if e.get('is_dir') else 1
                                else:
                                    return e['apparent'] if apparent else e['actual']
                            ents=sorted(ents, key=esz, reverse=True)
                        for ent in ents:
                            if count_flag:
                                sz=ent.get('file_count',0)+ent.get('dir_count',0) if ent.get('is_dir') else 1
                            else:
                                sz=ent['apparent'] if apparent else ent['actual']
                            size_str=str(sz) if bytes_flag or count_flag else human_size(sz)
                            full=os.path.join(cur_path, ent['name'])
                            if classify_flag and ent.get('is_dir'):
                                full_disp=full+'/'
                            else:
                                full_disp=full
                            print(f"{size_str:>8} {full_disp}")
                            if ent.get('is_dir'):
                                child=get_child(ent)
                                if child and depth<levels:
                                    print_full(child, full, depth+1)
                    print_full(dir_node, req_path.rstrip('/'), 1)
                else:
                    def get_child(ent):
                        if not ent.get('is_dir'):
                            return None
                        return get_dir_node(conn, ent['dev'], ent['ino'])
                    def print_tree(node, prefix_list, depth):
                        if depth>levels:
                            return
                        ents=node.get('entries',[])
                        if dirs_only:
                            ents=[e for e in ents if e.get('is_dir')]
                        if name_sort:
                            ents=sorted(ents, key=lambda e: e['name'].lower())
                        else:
                            def esz(e):
                                if count_flag:
                                    return e.get('file_count',0)+e.get('dir_count',0) if e.get('is_dir') else 1
                                else:
                                    return e['apparent'] if apparent else e['actual']
                            ents=sorted(ents, key=esz, reverse=True)
                        for i,ent in enumerate(ents):
                            is_last=i==len(ents)-1
                            if count_flag:
                                sz=ent.get('file_count',0)+ent.get('dir_count',0) if ent.get('is_dir') else 1
                            else:
                                sz=ent['apparent'] if apparent else ent['actual']
                            size_str=str(sz) if bytes_flag or count_flag else human_size(sz)
                            tree_pref=""
                            for last in prefix_list:
                                if ascii_flag:
                                    tree_pref+= "    " if last else "|   "
                                else:
                                    tree_pref+= "    " if last else "  │   "
                            child_node=get_child(ent)
                            has_children=child_node and len(child_node.get('entries',[]))>0
                            if ascii_flag:
                                if has_children:
                                    branch="`+- " if is_last else "|+- "
                                else:
                                    branch="`- " if is_last else "|- "
                            else:
                                if has_children:
                                    branch="╰┬─ " if is_last else "├┬─ "
                                else:
                                    branch="╰─ " if is_last else "├─ "
                            name_disp=ent['name']
                            if classify_flag and ent.get('is_dir'):
                                name_disp+='/'
                            print(f"{size_str:>8} {tree_pref}{branch}{name_disp}")
                            if ent.get('is_dir') and child_node and depth<levels:
                                print_tree(child_node, prefix_list+[is_last], depth+1)
                    print_tree(dir_node, [], 1)
    conn.close()
